artifacts.summary: Root-cause confirmation plus design recommendation for a topic-scoped literature coverage-delta guard extending the existing sparse-coverage machinery.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's literature extension, the global Literature/ index.json's .entries array mixes top-level documents (parent_doc == null) with their chunk children in one flat list, so `.entries | length` on the global index over-counts documents by roughly 2x relative to a doc-level count (measured: 414 total entries vs 204 parent_doc==null documents). Any code comparing a per-repo sub-index's doc-level entry count against the global index must filter to `select(.parent_doc == null)` on the global side or the comparison is not apples-to-apples.

literature-discover.sh's Tier 1 keyword matcher (filter_terms: stop-word/short-token filtering; term_matches: case-insensitive substring match; MULTI_TERM_MATCH_THRESHOLD for long queries) is the established, reusable pattern for matching a task description's terms against the global Literature index's title/keywords/summary fields. Prefer reusing this over writing a second keyword matcher for any new global-index-scanning feature (e.g. coverage-delta detection).

The literature extension's sparse-coverage family (literature-lit-flag-resolve.sh, literature-briefing.sh's lit-coverage marker) deliberately folds new failure signals into the EXISTING sparse boolean/directive rather than adding new unconsumed fields -- sparse-coverage.md states this explicitly as a design principle (a new flag nothing polls reproduces the exact silent-degradation bug the mechanism exists to prevent). Any new coverage-related signal in this subsystem should extend SPARSE_PROMPT_NEEDED / the lit-coverage marker rather than mint a parallel directive.
